adds.rationale: Freshly-listed pure-play space & missile-defense structures manufacturer gives fresh rockets/defense exposure to replace a lunar-lander name whose execution thesis just took a second hit.

news_evidence.summary: Karman Space & Defense priced its IPO at $22/share, began trading on the NYSE under KRMN on Feb 13, 2025, opened +30% above the IPO price, and raised over $500M; the company designs/manufactures mission-critical structures and propulsion components for missile-defense and space-launch programs.

removes.rationale: Second consecutive Intuitive Machines lunar lander tipped over on touchdown, undercutting the commercial-reliability thesis just as a competitor executed a clean soft landing days earlier in the same window.

news_evidence.summary: Intuitive Machines' Athena (IM-2) lander touched down near the lunar south pole on March 6, 2025 but tipped onto its side inside a crater after an altimeter failure — the same failure mode as IM-1; NASA confirmed lander operations ended roughly 13 hours later.

Firefly Aerospace's Blue Ghost Mission 1 achieved the first fully successful commercial Moon soft landing on March 2, 2025, meeting 100% of mission objectives — a direct contrast to Intuitive Machines' repeated landing troubles.

rationale_overall: One clean swap this quarter: LUNR exits after Athena's second consecutive lander tip-over (March 6) broke the commercial-reliability thesis just as Firefly's Blue Ghost showed the bar peers are clearing (March 2); KRMN enters on its Feb 13 IPO, adding differentiated missile-defense/space-structures exposure without over-stacking any single bucket (rockets_spacecraft holds at 3: RKLB, ASTS, KRMN). Everything else holds: IONQ is consolidating the quantum stack (ID Quantique agreement, EPB commercial quantum hub, ATM capital raised), OKLO is progressing through NRC pre-application review, WELL beat Q4-24 with same-store SHO NOI +23.9% YoY and raised 2025 guidance, TER is diversifying into robotics partnerships, and RKLB/ASTS/ITA carry the rest of the rockets and defense exposure. Symbotic's Walmart robotics deal was reviewed but skipped (TER already covers robotics; no negative signal to fund a second swap within the cap). The Jan 27 DeepSeek shock (NVDA -17%) is a reminder the AI wave is late-cycle and worth watching, but with no individually overweight AI name it doesn't yet clear the removal bar.
